data.title: World Brief · Saturday, November 7, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 19:05 ET

items.title: Democrats take both chambers of Congress
items.text: Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterms; the new Congress takes office in January. Vice President Vance largely blamed the defeat on the Iran war, while Trump signaled he is ready to fight the new majority. The risk of gridlock in 2027 over the budget, the debt ceiling and investigations is rising.

items.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm island again
items.text: Two missiles hit Qeshm, at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, on Friday night; Trump called it a "small" operation targeting an air-defense asset. According to UKMTO, 11 ships were attacked in the area last week and 3 sank; transits are ~65% below pre-war levels. Qatari mediation continues, and Iran has set 7 conditions for reopening the strait. This is the main risk for oil pricing.

items.title: Jobs surprise: +165,000 in October
items.text: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against expectations of ~59,000-65,000, and unemployment fell from 4.2% to 4.1%. The strong data reinforced expectations that the Fed will not rush to cut rates; yields and the dollar rose. Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51, and 1-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3%.

items.title: AI/chip sell-off: Nasdaq's worst week since June
items.text: The Nasdaq fell ~5.5% and the chip index ~12% on Thursday; despite Friday's rebound (AMD +11%), the Nasdaq ended the week down 3.4%. Concerns that new restrictions on data-center construction could follow the Democratic win weighed on AI investment expectations; the VIX is around 25.6.

items.title: Shooting in Krakow, Poland
items.text: On Saturday afternoon an attacker drove into the Main Market Square and opened fire at random: at least 6 people were killed and 15 wounded. The suspect, a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by police; no motive has been announced yet.

data.title: World Brief · Friday, November 6, 2026
data.subtitle: Prepared 18:59 ET

items.title: US jobs crush expectations
items.text: Nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 in October (consensus ~59,000) and unemployment came in at 4.1%. Markets now price a higher chance of a Fed rate hike in December, which feeds directly into short-term rates and currency risk.

items.title: Partial rebound after the AI sell-off
items.text: After the Nasdaq fell more than 5.5% on Thursday and entered correction territory, it recovered 1.1% today, led by chipmakers. In Asia, the Kospi and Nikkei plunged about 6%. The sell-off was triggered by fears of tighter regulation after AI-critical candidates won in the midterms.

items.title: Midterms: Congress flips to the Democrats
items.text: According to CBS and NBC, Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate; some races are still being counted. Jeffries expects at least 255 seats. Trump's 2027 agenda (taxes, budget, regulation) now has to pass a divided Congress.

items.title: Iran war: threats and diplomacy side by side
items.text: Trump said the US may have to destroy the rest of Iran; meanwhile, Iran has reportedly sent a nuclear proposal via Qatar that Washington is reviewing. Two tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent is holding near $98.

items.title: Corporate front
items.text: Oracle fell on reports that Microsoft ended a computing contract; Tesla will end Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-next year to make room for the Cybercab. Moderna beat third-quarter expectations and raised its 2026 revenue target.

items.text: Roughly $2 trillion was wiped off the Nasdaq. According to Reuters, hedge funds locked in profits on 2026's AI winners ahead of year-end, while retail investors were the biggest net sellers since 2020. The break in volatility and risk appetite could shape pricing and liquidity into year-end.

items.text: CBS projects Democrats at 54 or more Senate seats, with a comfortable House majority expected. Trump said he would accept the results and use his veto; Speaker Johnson will not run again for the GOP leadership. On the agenda for markets: debt-ceiling talks, investigations and limits on Iran policy.
items.title: Democrats win both chambers of Congress

items.text: Brent rebounded 3.9% to near $98 after a roughly 9% drop the day before. Trump said there are no new strike plans but the US is ready to escalate; the NYT reports Iran is reviewing nuclear proposals brokered by Qatar. The risk of tanker attacks in the Gulf remains.
items.title: Iran war and oil

items.text: The Bank of England raised rates for the first time since 2023 and, with a hawkish vote split, left the door open to more. Markets pushed the Fed's next hike to March, pricing about 40 bp of further tightening over the cycle. Brazil paused its cuts; Mexico delivered a surprise cut.

items.text: According to CBS, Democrats reached at least 54 Senate seats (with many seats flipping, including Texas, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina) and also won the House. Hakeem Jeffries will become the first Black Speaker of the House. Trump accepted the result but said he may veto legislation, which in practice means two years of divided government.

items.text: In Qatar-brokered talks, Iran called the US reply to its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz insufficient. Trump confirmed Tuesday's limited strike; US media report plans for broader post-election strikes. The direction of oil prices hinges on this.

items.text: Brent is down about 16% so far this week; defense (Lockheed -7%) and energy stocks were the biggest losers. With oil the main driver of inflation this year, the move also shifts Fed and ECB expectations.
items.title: Oil slump, energy stocks lag

items.text: Euro-area inflation rose to 4.0% in October; Bundesbank President Nagel said a December hike will probably be needed. Helped by this and a weaker dollar, the euro is at its strongest since early October.

items.text: CVS announced a plan to split in two; Microsoft rose 7% and McDonald's about 6%. Goldman said Democratic gains in the states make data-center moratoriums more likely, which could affect about 45% of planned capacity; CoreWeave fell 10%.
